Truncated Analytical Observed Hessian (Continuous)

Source: R/truncated.R
distrib_hessian.TruncatedContinuousDistrib.Rd

Computes $$\frac{\partial^2 \ell_T}{\partial\theta_i\partial\theta_j} = H_{ij}(y) - M_{ij} + m_i m_j, \qquad M_{ij} = \mathbb{E}_T[H_{ij} + s_i s_j],$$ the subtracted part being the second derivative of \(\log Z\). Only \(H_{ij}(y)\) varies with the data; the correction is one number per component, recycled to the length of y.

Arguments

distrib

A TruncatedContinuousDistrib object, from truncated().

y

A numeric vector of observations.

theta

A named list of the parent's parameters.

scale

One of "parameter" (the default) or "link", applied by the generic before dispatch.

...

Unused, and accepted so that the signature matches the generic's.

Value

A named list of numeric vectors of length length(y), one component per unordered pair of parameters, keyed as hess_names(distrib@params).

Notation

\(L\) and \(U\) are the truncation endpoints, both included in the support; \(Z(\theta) = P(L \le Y \le U)\) is the retained mass; \(f\) and \(F\) are the parent's density and distribution function; \(s_i\) and \(H_{ij}\) are the parent's score and observed Hessian; and \(\mathbb{E}_T\) is expectation under the truncated law.

See also

truncated(), trunc_hessian() for the shared body, trunc_M() for \(M_{ij}\), and distrib_expected_hessian.TruncatedContinuousDistrib() for the expectation.

Examples

tn <- truncated(gaussian1_distrib(), lower = -1, upper = 2)
theta <- list(mu = 0.3, sigma = 1.2)

y <- c(-0.5, 0, 1)
H <- distrib_hessian(tn, y, theta)
vapply(H, sum, numeric(1))
#>       mu_mu sigma_sigma    mu_sigma 
#>  -0.8721839   0.4749147   0.6374049 

# Against a numerical Hessian of the truncated log-likelihood.
ll <- function(v) {
  t2 <- as.list(v); names(t2) <- tn@params
  sum(distrib_pdf(tn, y, t2, log = TRUE))
}
Hn <- numDeriv::hessian(ll, unlist(theta))
ref <- vapply(distributions7:::hess_pairs(tn@params),
              function(q) Hn[match(q[1], tn@params), match(q[2], tn@params)],
              numeric(1))
max(abs(vapply(H, sum, numeric(1)) - ref))
#> [1] 6.119927e-11

# The correction is constant across observations.
round(unlist(H) - unlist(distrib_hessian(gaussian1_distrib(), y, theta)), 8)
#>       mu_mu1       mu_mu2       mu_mu3 sigma_sigma1 sigma_sigma2 sigma_sigma3 
#>   0.40371646   0.40371646   0.40371646   0.05220921   0.05220921   0.05220921 
#>    mu_sigma1    mu_sigma2    mu_sigma3 
#>   0.05814730   0.05814730   0.05814730
